name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run a controlled prompt variant audit for one week. Track every prompt change in a log, including the reason for the change and the expected impact. This gives us hard data on which tweaks actually move metrics, not just hunches. Trade-off: it adds short-term overhead to log changes, but the long-term clarity on what works beats guessing.

name: Gauge
text: The risk isn’t just overhead—it’s that logging every tweak turns the audit into a bureaucracy that slows iteration. A better alternative is to run a *sampled* audit: log only changes that cross a clear threshold (e.g., >5% metric shift or new failure mode), then verify the rest via weekly spot-checks. Settle it by running both for two weeks and comparing the signal-to-noise ratio in the data.
